bull_bear.body: Merger of AG Enviro completed Dec 2025 to optimize cash flow; Net debt target rising to 1.0-1.2x equity for expansions; Dividend policy under board review post-merger.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Elevated DSO (114 days, improved to 96 subsequently); Municipal payment delays; Execution risk on AP WtE land handover; Regulatory changes in wage codes.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term 20% CAGR despite Q3 softness; Emphasizes shift to high-margin processing/WtE; Cautious on client selection (municipalities) but optimistic on post-election execution speed.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: PCMC tipping fee escalated from Rs.505 to Rs.656/ton (cumulative catch-up); 90% of Thane project capex reimbursed milestone-based before operations, reducing balance sheet strain; C&D segment poised to double from 5% base due to policy shifts.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Leverage is presented as the headline discipline: Net Debt/Equity FY26 0.3x, having moved 0.1x (FY21) - 0.1x (FY22) - 0.5x (FY23) - 0.5x (FY24) - 0.4x (FY25) - 0.3 (FY26); the quarterly series shows 0.4x for Q1FY27 with a current ratio of 1.2x.
- Returns have compressed alongside a larger asset base: Capital Employed rose 591 - 704 - 969 - 1,133 - 1,292 - 1,308 (Rs in Cr, FY21-FY26) while RoCE moved 16.7% - 18.9% - 13.3% - 13.1% - 11.6% - 11.5% and RoE 14.5% - 17.0% - 13.7% - 13.9% - 12.3% - 10.0%.
- Credit ratings disclosed: Antony Waste Handling Cell - CARE BBB+; Stable on working capital limits (Rs 1,350 lakh) and CARE A3+ on bank guarantee (Rs 2,200 lakh); Antony Lara Enviro Solutions - Crisil A-/Watch Developing term loan (Rs 3,280 lakh); Antony Lara Renewable Energy - Crisil BBB+/Watch Developing term loan (Rs 15,200 lakh).
- Bidding capital is gated by an internal hurdle: "Financial viability aligned with internal hurdle rate for bidding" and "Detailed viability analysis of the project".
- Cash deployment history (consolidated cash flow): Net Cash from Investing Activities ran -260.4 (FY23), -150.7 (FY24) and -147.5 (FY25) before easing to -55.6 in FY26, with Net Cash from Financing Activities turning to -93.0 in FY26 from +11.5 in FY25.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- One of India's leading integrated MSW management organisations, operating across the full circular-waste value chain from collection to waste-to-energy
- High-performance operational platform: fleet of over 2,600 specialised vehicles and state-of-the-art processing plants
- Long-term management of Kanjurmarg, described as one of Asia's largest engineered landfill facilities
- Established, long-term trusted partner to urban local bodies and municipal authorities, with 40+ executed/ongoing projects and relationships with 25+ ULBs/institutional clients since inception
- 25-year operating track record (founded 2001) with proven delivery on large-scale municipal contracts
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Concentration on public-sector municipal counterparties — Customers are Urban Local Bodies, Municipal Corporations and Cantonment Boards operating within state-defined fiscal frameworks; the AR states this 'distinct nature of our customer base shapes our approach to financial stewardship, contract management and long-term partnership development,' implying revenue realisation and payment timing are tied to public-sector budget and governance cycles rather than diversified private-sector demand.
- Long-tenure concession/contract risk with Urban Local Bodies — The Company explicitly flags that it must 'manage contractual, operational, and business risks associated with long-term engagements with ULBs and other stakeholders through performance oversight, proactive engagement, and appropriate contractual arrangements' — multi-decade concessions concentrate execution and renewal risk with government counterparties.
- Workforce and community health & safety exposure — Operations are described as involving 'complex and evolving challenges,' with an explicit commitment to 'safeguarding the health, safety, and well-being of our employees, contractors, and communities'; mitigation relies on mandatory training, safety procedures and monitoring, indicating safety is treated as a material, actively managed operational risk.
- Regulatory and compliance risk across a multi-dimensional ERM framework — The Risk Management Policy/framework spans 'strategic, operational, financial, compliance, environmental, social, and governance dimensions,' overseen by the Board and Risk Management Committee, reflecting exposure to evolving environmental, licensing and municipal-services regulation that the Company must continuously track and adapt to.
- Escalating, unquantified risk register — Risks are internally ranked Low/Medium/High and 'high-priority risks are escalated to the Risk Management Committee for timely review and action,' but the routed text does not enumerate the specific named risks in this register, limiting external visibility into which risks are currently rated highest.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: C&T: Rs.175cr (+7% YoY), 0.53M tons; Processing: Rs.66cr (+12% YoY), 0.88M tons; WtE: Shutdown in Q3, normalized ops expected Q4; C&D: ~5% revenue share, EBITDA neutral currently.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Claims market leadership in Indian municipal solid waste: "Leading Player in SWM Industry", "25 Years of Operational Excellence", "4.82 Mn+ Household & other Establishments Served Everyday", "25+ Municipal Corps & conglomerate worked, since inception" and "10 States (Projects executed till date)".
- Says it "Operates Largest Single location waste processing plant in Asia" at Kanjurmarg, where "~90% Processing of waste generated in Mumbai" is handled; the slide separately states "Total waste generated in Mumbai is handled at Kanjurmarg site 90%".
- Contract book is long-dated: "Currently 19 on-going contracts" in MSW C&T with "Average on-going contract duration is 7.7 years", and "6 Waste Processing and 1 C&D ongoing contracts" with "Average on-going contract duration is 23 years".
- De-risking framework rests on client selection - "Focus on municipal corporations with strong financials/ credit ratings" - plus user-fee collection from waste generators in NOIDA, Jhansi and Varanasi to reduce collection risk, and "Financial viability aligned with internal hurdle rate for bidding".
- Cluster-based bidding: "11 on-going projects in MMR" and "6 on-going projects in NCR", with intent to "Continue to focus on bidding projects in new states in clusters to increase profitability and efficiency".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Group structure] Several operating entities are part-owned: Antony Lara Enviro Solutions is AW 73% | Lara Central, Brazil 27%; Antony Lara Renewable is AW 49% | AL 51%; Kadapa and Kurnool Renew Energy are AL 75% | JFE, Japan 25%; Mumbai Eco Solutions is AW 51% | Jigar Transport 29% | MK Ent. 20%; Varanasi Waste Solutions is AW 98% | Kerzellion 2%. Minority interest is material - Non-Controlling Interest equity of Rs 176.3 cr as at Mar-26.
- [Contract-exit obligations] "For projects on operation and maintenance basis, entire vehicle fleet is required to be returned to municipality (not required for DBOO & BOO contracts)" and "For projects involving landfills, requirement of restoring the land to its original condition at company's own cost".
- [Exceptional item] The FY-series P&L footnote records an "Exceptional item of Rs 23.9 crores on the account of settlement from arbitration", shown in FY25 as (23.9).
- [Industry backdrop] Deck cites waste generation rising 60 to 95 mn TPA (FY21-FY26, CAGR 9.6%) and the MSW market 41.0 to 70.0 INR bn (CAGR 11.3%), plus an India waste management market of 1,211 (2025) to 1,714 (2030) at 7.2% CAGR; it also notes India's 77% open dumping versus a global mix of 52% landfill / 25% recycled / 13% WtE / 10% compost.
- [Client quality] All-India Swachh Survekshan 2025 rankings of client cities are used as proof of execution - Pimpri Chinchwad 07th, Thane 15th, Varanasi 17th, Nashik 22nd, Nagpur 27th, Delhi 31st (>10 Lakh population); Panvel 06th and Jhansi 17th (<10 Lakh); Navi Mumbai and Noida as "Super Swachh League City".
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: AWHCL covers the entire municipal solid waste (MSW) value chain — door-to-door collection, transportation, mechanised sweeping, segregation, processing, resource recovery, waste-to-energy generation, landfill management and legacy waste (bio-mining) remediation — primarily for urban local bodies, municipal corporations and government institutions. It also operates a non-municipal commercial/institutional hygiene brand, Click2Clean, through wholly-owned subsidiary Antony Recycling Private Limited. Its flagship asset is the long-term management of the Kanjurmarg engineered sanitary landfill and waste processing facility in Mumbai, described as one of Asia's largest.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Collection & Transportation:** Door-to-door municipal solid waste collection, Mechanised road sweeping, Construction & demolition waste collection and transportation
- **Waste Processing / Resource Recovery:** Materials recovery, Composting, RDF (refuse-derived fuel) processing
- **Waste-to-Energy:** Waste-to-energy power generation from municipal solid waste
- **Bio Mining / Legacy Waste:** Legacy waste bio-mining and landfill remediation
- **Hygiene Solutions (Click2Clean brand):** Commercial, industrial, residential and institutional hygiene/cleaning services

latest_quarter.body: Q3 margin pressure from annual employee appraisals (fixed cost ~18% in C&T, ~45-50% in Processing); Fuel & labor constitute 61-64% of C&T costs; WtE margins >40% at steady state.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue growth: 15-18% for FY27, 20% long-term CAGR; Margin: 22-23% target (core); Order inflow: Focus on processing & WtE; Capex: Rs.600-650cr for AP WtE projects (75:25 debt/equity).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs.1,330cr potential over 7 years from 2 BMC C&T contracts (51% stake in consortium); 10-year Thane DBOT (Rs.67cr reimbursable capex); 2x AP WtE projects (750 TPD each, revenue from FY29).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: AP WtE projects (FY29 onset); Tamil Nadu & Eastern India WtE tenders; C&D segment doubling expected in FY27; Non-municipal B2C 'Click-to-clean' & EPR markets under evaluation.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Continue to invest in advanced technologies, strengthen Waste-to-Energy and recycling capabilities, enhance resource recovery and build resilient infrastructure
- Lead India's transition towards cleaner, smarter and more circular cities through innovation, digitalisation, operational excellence and responsible expansion
- Pursue technology partnerships for Waste-to-Energy (e.g., April 2026 agreements with JFE Engineering Corporation, Japan) to enable technology transfer, global best practices and enhanced project execution capability
- Diversify into the non-municipal commercial/institutional hygiene segment via the Click2Clean brand under subsidiary Antony Recycling
- Strengthen governance, risk oversight, safety and climate-adaptation practices following the July 2026 incident at the PCMC facility in Pune
- Dividends are paid out of the year's profits under a Board-adopted Dividend Distribution Policy (per SEBI Listing Regulations Regulation 43A); FY2025-26 saw the company's maiden dividend declaration, timed to its 25th/Silver Jubilee year, which management frames as reflecting confidence built through consistent performance, prudent financial stewardship and responsible capital allocation. No buyback, debt-reduction target or credit-rating commentary is present in this routed text.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: AWHCL describes a disciplined, multi-year 'manufactured capital enhancement programme' targeting throughput expansion, recovery-yield improvement and operational cost reduction across its processing infrastructure, with capacity augmentation at MRF and RDF facilities, fleet upgradation, and integration of advanced segregation and densification technologies underway. During the year, investments were directed towards facility upgrades, fleet modernisation, process automation, digital monitoring systems and environmental management infrastructure. Named project-level expansion during the year: two ~15 MW Waste-to-Energy projects in Kadapa and Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh (awarded by NREDCAP August 2025, 20-year concessions, under construction via wholly-owned SPVs incorporated September 2025); a 600-800 TPD municipal solid waste pre-processing/Material Recovery Facility project awarded by Thane Municipal Corporation (10-year concession); collection & transportation contracts (~1,250 TPD) awarded by BMC in December 2025, executed via SPV Mumbai Eco Solutions Private Limited (51% AWHCL stake); and a CIDCO bio-mining contract (~8.60 lakh tonnes of legacy waste at Taloja MIDC) nearing completion at year-end. The company also entered a technology collaboration (April 2026) with JFE Engineering Corporation, Japan for the Kadapa/Kurnool WTE SPVs, alongside an existing Waste-to-Energy technology partnership with Kanadevia (formerly Hitachi Zosen). Management describes a 'strong order book and a robust pipeline of infrastructure investments' across C&T, MRF, RDF, WtE and bio-mining, with each project assessed against tipping-fee adequacy, capital payback and contractual risk allocation before commitment, and investment decisions anchored to SWM Rules, 2026 mandates.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's rapid urbanisation, growing focus on resource efficiency and commitment to a circular economy are reshaping the waste management landscape
- Waste-to-energy initiatives are positioned to contribute to India's transition to cleaner energy systems by supporting landfill diversion, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and advancing circular resource utilisation
- Growth driven by new municipal/ULB contract wins and concessions across collection & transportation, pre-processing/MRF, bio-mining and waste-to-energy
- Executed and ongoing projects across 10 states in partnership with numerous Urban Local Bodies, spanning collection, transportation, processing, recycling, Waste-to-Energy and resource recovery
- Thane Municipal Corporation pre-processing project (600-800 TPD MSW, Material Recovery Facility) secured during the year, 10-year concession
- Two ~15 MW Waste-to-Energy projects awarded in Andhra Pradesh (Kadapa and Kurnool) by NREDCAP in August 2025, each with a 20-year concession, under construction via dedicated SPVs
- Two BMC collection & transportation projects (~1,250 TPD) won in December 2025 as consortium leader with Jigar Transport and M.K. Enterprises, executed via SPV Mumbai Eco Solutions Private Limited
- CIDCO bio-mining contract (~8.60 lakh tonnes of legacy waste, Taloja MIDC) secured in 2024, nearing completion as at year-end
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: AWHCL delivered steady 9% Q3 revenue growth driven by volume escalation, though margins dipped to 18.4% due to seasonal employee costs and a 82-day WtE plant shutdown. The strategic merger of AG Enviro and new wins (Rs.1,330cr BMC C&T, Rs.67cr Thane DBOT, two AP WtE projects) secure a 20% CAGR trajectory with improved cash flow visibility from FY29.

risks.note: Customers are Urban Local Bodies, Municipal Corporations and Cantonment Boards operating within state-defined fiscal frameworks; the AR states this 'distinct nature of our customer base shapes our approach to financial stewardship, contract management and long-term partnership development,' implying revenue realisation and payment timing are tied to public-sector budget and governance cycles rather than diversified private-sector demand.

risks.risk: Long-tenure concession/contract risk with Urban Local Bodies
risks.note: The Company explicitly flags that it must 'manage contractual, operational, and business risks associated with long-term engagements with ULBs and other stakeholders through performance oversight, proactive engagement, and appropriate contractual arrangements' — multi-decade concessions concentrate execution and renewal risk with government counterparties.

risks.risk: Workforce and community health & safety exposure
risks.note: Operations are described as involving 'complex and evolving challenges,' with an explicit commitment to 'safeguarding the health, safety, and well-being of our employees, contractors, and communities'; mitigation relies on mandatory training, safety procedures and monitoring, indicating safety is treated as a material, actively managed operational risk.

risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance risk across a multi-dimensional ERM framework
risks.note: The Risk Management Policy/framework spans 'strategic, operational, financial, compliance, environmental, social, and governance dimensions,' overseen by the Board and Risk Management Committee, reflecting exposure to evolving environmental, licensing and municipal-services regulation that the Company must continuously track and adapt to.

Risks are internally ranked Low/Medium/High and 'high-priority risks are escalated to the Risk Management Committee for timely review and action,' but the routed text does not enumerate the specific named risks in this register, limiting external visibility into which risks are currently rated highest.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Antony Waste Handling Cell Limited (AWHCL) is one of India's leading integrated municipal solid waste management organisations, delivering collection, transportation, processing, resource recovery and waste-to-energy services to urban local bodies across India.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: AWHCL covers the entire municipal solid waste (MSW) value chain — door-to-door collection, transportation, mechanised sweeping, segregation, processing, resource recovery, waste-to-energy generation, landfill management and legacy waste (bio-mining) remediation — primarily for urban local bodies, municipal corporations and government institutions. It also operates a non-municipal commercial/institutional hygiene brand, Click2Clean, through wholly-owned subsidiary Antony Recycling Private Limited. Its flagship asset is the long-term management of the Kanjurmarg engineered sanitary landfill and waste processing facility in Mumbai, described as one of Asia's largest.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- AL Waste Bio Remediation LLP — subsidiary: 86.23% held by AWHCL; participates in BRSR initiatives
- Antony Lara Enviro Solutions Private Limited — subsidiary: 73.00% held by AWHCL; material subsidiary; established through partnership with Lara Central De Tratamento de Residuos Limited, Brazil; operates the Kanjurmarg Integrated Waste Management Project, Mumbai
- Antony Lara Renewable Energy Private Limited — subsidiary: 86.23% held by AWHCL; material subsidiary; SPV jointly established with Antony Lara Enviro Solutions to develop/operate the PCMC Waste-to-Energy facility at Moshi, Pune
- Antony Recycling Private Limited — subsidiary: 100% wholly-owned subsidiary; operates the Click2Clean commercial/institutional hygiene solutions brand
- Varanasi Waste Solutions Private Limited — subsidiary: 98.00% held by AWHCL; SPV for integrated MSW management (collection, transportation, sweeping) in Varanasi
- Kadapa Renew Energy Private Limited — subsidiary: 73.00% held by AWHCL (via Antony Lara Enviro Solutions); wholly-owned SPV incorporated September 1, 2025 for a Waste-to-Energy project in Kadapa, Andhra Pradesh; yet to commence commercial operations
- Kurnool Renew Energy Private Limited — subsidiary: 73.00% held by AWHCL (via Antony Lara Enviro Solutions); wholly-owned SPV incorporated September 2, 2025 for a Waste-to-Energy project in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh; yet to commence commercial operations
- Mumbai Eco Solutions Private Limited — subsidiary: 51.00% held by AWHCL; SPV incorporated for execution of BMC collection & transportation projects; yet to commence operations
- AG Enviro Infra Projects Private Limited — subsidiary (ceased): Former wholly-owned subsidiary; merged by absorption into AWHCL effective December 31, 2025 pursuant to NCLT order dated December 18, 2025; ceased to exist
- Mazaya Waste Management LLC — associate/JV: 49% held per BRSR (50% per related-party note); company does not expect returns on the investment, has provided for diminution in value, and has applied to RBI for permission to write off the entire investment; not consolidated due to non-availability of financial information
- Home Management and Care Givers Sector Skill Council — associate: Section 8 (not-for-profit) company; 20.00% ownership interest held by the group
- Antony Motors Private Limited — related party: Other related entity per Companies Act, 2013 (does not meet Ind AS 24 related-party definition)
- Antony Garages Private Limited — related party: Other related entity per Companies Act, 2013 (does not meet Ind AS 24 related-party definition)
- Antony Commercial Vehicles Private Limited — related party: Other related entity per Companies Act, 2013 (does not meet Ind AS 24 related-party definition)
- Antony Waste Handling Cell Limited Employees Group Gratuity Scheme — related party: Post-employment benefit plan
- AWHCL Employee Welfare Trust — related party: Trust

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: C&T: Rs.175cr (+7% YoY), 0.53M tons; Processing: Rs.66cr (+12% YoY), 0.88M tons; WtE: Shutdown in Q3, normalized ops expected Q4; C&D: ~5% revenue share, EBITDA neutral currently.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Collection & Transportation:** Door-to-door municipal solid waste collection, Mechanised road sweeping, Construction & demolition waste collection and transportation
- **Waste Processing / Resource Recovery:** Materials recovery, Composting, RDF (refuse-derived fuel) processing
- **Waste-to-Energy:** Waste-to-energy power generation from municipal solid waste
- **Bio Mining / Legacy Waste:** Legacy waste bio-mining and landfill remediation
- **Hygiene Solutions (Click2Clean brand):** Commercial, industrial, residential and institutional hygiene/cleaning services

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Urban local bodies and municipal corporations in Maharashtra (Mumbai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Pimpri-Chinchwad, Pune, Nashik, Nagpur, Panvel)
- Andhra Pradesh (Kadapa, Kurnool) via NREDCAP-awarded waste-to-energy projects
- Delhi-NCR and Uttar Pradesh (Delhi, Noida, Greater Noida, Jhansi, Varanasi)
- Non-municipal commercial and institutional hygiene sector (Click2Clean brand, 150+ accounts)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Rs.1,330cr potential over 7 years from 2 BMC C&T contracts (51% stake in consortium); 10-year Thane DBOT (Rs.67cr reimbursable capex); 2x AP WtE projects (750 TPD each, revenue from FY29).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth: 15-18% for FY27, 20% long-term CAGR; Margin: 22-23% target (core); Order inflow: Focus on processing & WtE; Capex: Rs.600-650cr for AP WtE projects (75:25 debt/equity).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: AP WtE projects (FY29 onset); Tamil Nadu & Eastern India WtE tenders; C&D segment doubling expected in FY27; Non-municipal B2C 'Click-to-clean' & EPR markets under evaluation.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's rapid urbanisation, growing focus on resource efficiency and commitment to a circular economy are reshaping the waste management landscape
- Waste-to-energy initiatives are positioned to contribute to India's transition to cleaner energy systems by supporting landfill diversion, reducing greenhouse gas emissions and advancing circular resource utilisation
- Growth driven by new municipal/ULB contract wins and concessions across collection & transportation, pre-processing/MRF, bio-mining and waste-to-energy
- Executed and ongoing projects across 10 states in partnership with numerous Urban Local Bodies, spanning collection, transportation, processing, recycling, Waste-to-Energy and resource recovery
- Thane Municipal Corporation pre-processing project (600-800 TPD MSW, Material Recovery Facility) secured during the year, 10-year concession
- Two ~15 MW Waste-to-Energy projects awarded in Andhra Pradesh (Kadapa and Kurnool) by NREDCAP in August 2025, each with a 20-year concession, under construction via dedicated SPVs
- Two BMC collection & transportation projects (~1,250 TPD) won in December 2025 as consortium leader with Jigar Transport and M.K. Enterprises, executed via SPV Mumbai Eco Solutions Private Limited
- CIDCO bio-mining contract (~8.60 lakh tonnes of legacy waste, Taloja MIDC) secured in 2024, nearing completion as at year-end

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q3 margin pressure from annual employee appraisals (fixed cost ~18% in C&T, ~45-50% in Processing); Fuel & labor constitute 61-64% of C&T costs; WtE margins >40% at steady state.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Merger of AG Enviro completed Dec 2025 to optimize cash flow; Net debt target rising to 1.0-1.2x equity for expansions; Dividend policy under board review post-merger.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: AWHCL describes a disciplined, multi-year 'manufactured capital enhancement programme' targeting throughput expansion, recovery-yield improvement and operational cost reduction across its processing infrastructure, with capacity augmentation at MRF and RDF facilities, fleet upgradation, and integration of advanced segregation and densification technologies underway. During the year, investments were directed towards facility upgrades, fleet modernisation, process automation, digital monitoring systems and environmental management infrastructure. Named project-level expansion during the year: two ~15 MW Waste-to-Energy projects in Kadapa and Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh (awarded by NREDCAP August 2025, 20-year concessions, under construction via wholly-owned SPVs incorporated September 2025); a 600-800 TPD municipal solid waste pre-processing/Material Recovery Facility project awarded by Thane Municipal Corporation (10-year concession); collection & transportation contracts (~1,250 TPD) awarded by BMC in December 2025, executed via SPV Mumbai Eco Solutions Private Limited (51% AWHCL stake); and a CIDCO bio-mining contract (~8.60 lakh tonnes of legacy waste at Taloja MIDC) nearing completion at year-end. The company also entered a technology collaboration (April 2026) with JFE Engineering Corporation, Japan for the Kadapa/Kurnool WTE SPVs, alongside an existing Waste-to-Energy technology partnership with Kanadevia (formerly Hitachi Zosen). Management describes a 'strong order book and a robust pipeline of infrastructure investments' across C&T, MRF, RDF, WtE and bio-mining, with each project assessed against tipping-fee adequacy, capital payback and contractual risk allocation before commitment, and investment decisions anchored to SWM Rules, 2026 mandates.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on long-term 20% CAGR despite Q3 softness; Emphasizes shift to high-margin processing/WtE; Cautious on client selection (municipalities) but optimistic on post-election execution speed.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- One of India's leading integrated MSW management organisations, operating across the full circular-waste value chain from collection to waste-to-energy
- High-performance operational platform: fleet of over 2,600 specialised vehicles and state-of-the-art processing plants
- Long-term management of Kanjurmarg, described as one of Asia's largest engineered landfill facilities
- Established, long-term trusted partner to urban local bodies and municipal authorities, with 40+ executed/ongoing projects and relationships with 25+ ULBs/institutional clients since inception
- 25-year operating track record (founded 2001) with proven delivery on large-scale municipal contracts

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Elevated DSO (114 days, improved to 96 subsequently); Municipal payment delays; Execution risk on AP WtE land handover; Regulatory changes in wage codes.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: PCMC tipping fee escalated from Rs.505 to Rs.656/ton (cumulative catch-up); 90% of Thane project capex reimbursed milestone-based before operations, reducing balance sheet strain; C&D segment poised to double from 5% base due to policy shifts.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue to invest in advanced technologies, strengthen Waste-to-Energy and recycling capabilities, enhance resource recovery and build resilient infrastructure
- Lead India's transition towards cleaner, smarter and more circular cities through innovation, digitalisation, operational excellence and responsible expansion
- Pursue technology partnerships for Waste-to-Energy (e.g., April 2026 agreements with JFE Engineering Corporation, Japan) to enable technology transfer, global best practices and enhanced project execution capability
- Diversify into the non-municipal commercial/institutional …

challenges.body:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for efficient legacy dump remediation and municipal bond funding | Antony Waste Handling Cell Ltd | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of Union Budget's municipal bond incentives and Rs.100cr tranche support; awarded major BMC and Thane contracts aligning with 'Lakshya Zero Dumpsites' goal. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Group structure] Several operating entities are part-owned: Antony Lara Enviro Solutions is AW 73% | Lara Central, Brazil 27%; Antony Lara Renewable is AW 49% | AL 51%; Kadapa and Kurnool Renew Energy are AL 75% | JFE, Japan 25%; Mumbai Eco Solutions is AW 51% | Jigar Transport 29% | MK Ent. 20%; Varanasi Waste Solutions is AW 98% | Kerzellion 2%. Minority interest is material - Non-Controlling Interest equity of Rs 176.3 cr as at Mar-26.
- [Contract-exit obligations] "For projects on operation and maintenance basis, entire vehicle fleet is required to be returned to municipality (not required for DBOO & BOO contracts)" and "For projects involving landfills, requirement of restoring the land to its original condition at company's own cost".
- [Exceptional item] The FY-series P&L footnote records an "Exceptional item of Rs 23.9 crores on the account of settlement from arbitration", shown in FY25 as (23.9).
- [Industry backdrop] Deck cites waste generation rising 60 to 95 mn TPA (FY21-FY26, CAGR 9.6%) and the MSW market 41.0 to 70.0 INR bn (CAGR 11.3%), plus an India waste management market of 1,211 (2025) to 1,714 (2030) at 7.2% CAGR; it also notes India's 77% open dumping versus a global mix of 52% landfill / 25% recycled / 13% WtE / 10% compost.
- [Client quality] All-India Swachh Survekshan 2025 rankings of client cities are used as proof of execution - Pimpri Chinchwad 07th, Thane 15th, Varanasi 17th, Nashik 22nd, Nagpur 27th, Delhi 31st (>10 Lakh population); Panvel 06th and Jhansi 17th (<10 Lakh); Navi Mumbai and Noida as "Super Swachh League City".

themes.title: Water & environmental-infra EPC
themes.need: AMRUT, Namami Gange and Jal Jeevan still define the pipeline, but Q1FY27 put a number on the funding freeze. WPIL's consolidated revenue rose 32% to INR 501cr while STANDALONE collapsed 37% to INR 115cr as domestic Jal Jeevan invoicing froze, with INR 300-350cr of JJM receivables pending (mostly West Bengal, some MP) and nil received in the quarter - management expects substantial inflow only in Q2/H2. The offsetting discovery is that the theme has quietly become international: WPIL's overseas revenue roughly doubled to INR 386cr, about 77% of consolidated, on PCI Africa's first full execution quarter plus Gruppo Aturia MENA demand, lifting consolidated EBITDA margin to 15.04%. EIEL carries an all-time-high order book (~6x revenue); WABAG on desalination/technology; JISLJALEQS/JISLDVREQS and MAHEPC add micro-irrigation and water-efficiency equipment; EMSLIMITED/SPMLINFRA/JASH/DENTA/ELECTCAST/AWHCL add sewerage, control equipment and ductile-iron piping. Execution conversion, not order intake, remains the binding constraint.
themes.driver: JJM/AMRUT fund releases unlocking billing (WPIL's INR 300-350cr receivable is the tracer); FY27 order inflow; desalination + NTPC BESS EPC ramp; international Africa/MENA execution.
